Claude is free inside its box.
What leaves it goes through you.

The sandbox, the supervisor and the approval, on one page.

One idea: Claude can do anything inside the repo, but nothing that runs outside the box changes without your « yes ».

1The picture

you the Mac, outside the box the box (the sandbox) Claude's work

2The parts

  1. The sandbox: a box around Claude.
    • macOS enforces it (safehouse, rules in sandbox.sb): whatever is not allowed is refused.
    • It guards against an oops, not against a hostile agent.
  2. Claude: writes, tests, commits, in the repo.
    • Every proposal becomes a commit.
    • It cannot write the approved copy: that is outside its box.
  3. The supervisor (bin/claude-supervise): a bash program, not an AI.
    • It starts Claude in the box, then watches two things: your approval, and a restart request.
    • Between two turns, with no agent running, it stops Claude and resumes the same conversation.
  4. The approved copy (~/.config/site_perso/host): the code that runs outside the box.
    • Makefile, sandbox rules, Mac scripts: as they are at the last commit you approved.
    • A commit of Claude's gets in only through your « yes ».
  5. sandbox-apply: the door.
    • It shows what changes (in words first, approval.md, then the diff) and waits for your yes.
    • From the phone (the Shortcut goes through klar) or the Mac.
  6. comment-wake: the doorbell.
    • A comment of yours in the CRM, or a request from another repo, wakes the session.

3One approval, step by step

  1. Claude changes code that runs on the Mac, commits it, and writes in words what it changes for you.
  2. You: open /approve, read, tap « Approuver ».
  3. sandbox-apply copies that commit into the approved copy and records its number.
  4. The supervisor sees the number change; it waits for Claude's turn and its agents to finish.
  5. It stops Claude, then starts it again on the new code, in the same conversation.
  6. Claude resumes, checks that what needed the restart works, and carries on.

4Why it is built this way

  1. An oops does not spread.
    • Claude works freely; a mistake stays in the repo, where git undoes it.
  2. One tap, nothing more.
    • No restart by hand, no command to paste: the supervisor does it.
  3. Each repo has its own.
    • No shared rule: each its own box, and the repos pass rules to each other through their to_process/ inbox.

5What prevents forgetting

  1. Checks, not memory.
    • approval-guard: no approval link when nothing waits, always phone and Mac.
    • sandbox_rules: every new rule says what each other repo gets.
    • approved-test: an unapproved commit does not run on the Mac.
